input.reasoning_summary:
After investigating potential challenges, the initial SUPPORTED verdict remains correct. 

H1 challenged whether net income was actually positive. This is REFUTED by E10, which shows net income of $112.2 billion for Q2 2026, confirming positive net income that could be "boosted" by the equity gains.

H2 challenged whether the equity gains might be considered part of operating performance. NO_RELEVANT_EVIDENCE was found to support this challenge. The original evidence clearly shows these gains appear in "Other Income (Expense), Net" which is separate from operating income, and no evidence suggests they are considered part of operating performance.

H3 challenged whether net income was actually boosted on a net basis. This is REFUTED by the evidence showing net income increased from $28.2 billion in Q2 2025 (E11) to $112.2 billion in Q2 2026 (E10), an increase of approximately $84 billion. Given that equity security gains were $99 billion (E5), net income was clearly boosted substantially.

The evidence review confirms E5 as ENTAILS with EXACT_MATCH period compatibility and HISTORICAL_FACT statement time, directly supporting the claim that Q2 2026 net income was boosted by $99 billion in equity security gains. The presentation of these gains in OI&E (outside operating income) supports the interpretive assertion that they "do not reflect operating performance."

All challenges have been refuted or found to lack supporting evidence, confirming the initial verdict.
